needs.title: Daughter studying in the UK
needs.description: Her daughter Layla plans to study in the UK in about 3 years. Tuition and living costs will be around GBP 50,000 a year (roughly QAR 230,000 to 250,000), paid in pounds for 3 to 4 years.
needs.revealWhen: The student asks what 'the children's future' means specifically, about timelines, where the children will study, or which currency the costs will be in.
exampleQuestions: When you say your children's future, what exactly are you planning for?
Where and when are they likely to study, and in what currency will you be paying?

needs.title: Will not risk her capital
needs.description: She lost about QAR 120,000 investing in shares in 2020 and will not accept any product where her capital could fall in value. She reacts strongly against investment funds.
needs.revealWhen: The student asks about her attitude to risk, past investment experience, or how she would feel if the value went down, or the student recommends an investment fund.
exampleQuestions: Have you invested before? How did that go?
How would you feel if the value of your savings went down for a while?

needs.title: Needs some money available quickly
needs.description: Wants part of her savings available at short notice for emergencies, rather than all of it locked away for a long term.
needs.revealWhen: The student asks about access to her money, flexibility, or what would happen in an emergency.
exampleQuestions: How quickly might you need to get to some of this money?
Do you want to keep some of it available for emergencies?

needs.title: Son will study abroad too
needs.description: Her son Omar is two years younger and is likely to study abroad too, so the plan needs to cover both children, with costs overlapping for a few years.
needs.revealWhen: The student asks about the rest of the family, whether the plan should cover both children, or the longer-term picture.
exampleQuestions: Should this plan cover both of your children?
What does the next six or seven years look like for the family?

suitable.reason: Lets her build up pounds gradually ahead of tuition payments, reducing exchange-rate surprises, and pay the university directly in GBP.
Low-risk growth on savings that are currently earning nothing. Splitting it across 3, 6 and 12-month terms keeps part of the money close to maturity for emergencies.

unsuitable.reason: Her capital would be at risk, which she has ruled out after her 2020 losses, and the 5-year recommended holding period is longer than her 3-year need.
She has no debts to consolidate.
A business product; not relevant to her personal goals.
